## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the pill run logic, the new theme keys and the `--blend` text-colour sampler behave as described. The PR's JS assertions and `bar-text-color-test.sh` pass on this head and fail on the base. One exception to "unchanged unless enabled" was found in source: with pills off, the anchored centre widget (the clock) can move by 1 px. With pills on, a few colour and layout gaps remain, mostly around `"pill": false`.

### Pills off: the anchored centre widget can move 1 px

`shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:1671` and `:1726` replace `anchors.centerIn: parent` with `Math.round((P - (s - pillLead - pillTrail)) / 2) - pillLead`. The comment above them says this equals `anchors.centerIn` without pills. Qt's `centerIn` (`qquickanchors.cpp`, with the default `alignWhenCentered`) rounds each half separately: `qRound(P/2) - qRound(s/2)`. The two results differ by 1 whenever the parent size is even and the widget size is odd.

The stock vertical clock is 3 lines × `icon-slot` 27 = 81 px tall, so a left or right bar on an even-height output hits this case:

```text
left/right bar, output height P = 1080, stock vertical clock s = 81, pills unset

base  anchors.centerIn     qRound(1080/2) - qRound(81/2)  = 540 - 41 = 499
head  Math.round((P-s)/2)  Math.round(999/2)              = 500
```

The clock and the centre widgets anchored to it sit 1 px lower. On horizontal bars the same shift happens only when the clock width is an odd integer, which is not the typical case.

**Impact:** small, but it contradicts the "0 differing pixels at all four positions" claim for left and right bars at the default font size. This comes from source and Qt's anchor code; no screenshot diff was taken.

**Suggested change:** `x: Math.round(parent.width / 2) - Math.round((width - pillLead - pillTrail) / 2) - pillLead` (and the `y` equivalent). This reproduces `centerIn` exactly with pills off and keeps the anchor fixed when roles change.

### `"pill": false` widgets and tray icons do not get their own text colour

With pills on, `barForeground` becomes the pill text colour for the whole bar (`Bar.qml:102-104`). The tray's symbolic icons, however, read `bar.foreground`, which stays on the theme text colour (`widgets/Tray.qml:19`, `Bar.qml:77`):

```text
bar.barForeground (pill-aware) -> every WidgetButton, ActiveWindow, media,
                                  including widgets with "pill": false
bar.foreground (theme text)    -> tray symbolic icons (MultiEffect colorization)
```

- A `"pill": false` widget sits on the bar or the wallpaper, not on a pill, yet uses the colour picked for the pill. Example: the README layout (`transparent: true`, section pills, `omarchy.power` with `"pill": false`) over a light wallpaper. The default opaque pill keeps light text, so the bare power widget gets light text on the light wallpaper. Without pills the sampler would pick dark text there.
- A theme with a `[bar] pill-text` that differs from `[bar] text`, or a light `[bar] pill` on a dark theme, flips widget text and the tray chevron. The symbolic tray icons keep the theme text colour, so they can end up light on a light pill.

**Impact:** low-contrast text or icons in these theme and wallpaper combinations. Stock themes with default pill colours are mostly unaffected. This comes from the source; it was not observed on screen.

**Suggested change:** choose the foreground per slot (the pill colour for slots with a pill role, the pre-pill colour for role `none`), and have the tray use the pill-aware colour for its bar-facing icons. If per-slot colour is out of scope, document that `"pill": false` widgets share the pill's text colour.

### Pills on: a bare widget at a section end overhangs the bar

`sectionEndMargin` is `pillInset - Math.round(pillGap / 2)` (`Bar.qml:110`), which is 2 − 3 = −1 px at defaults. Pill slots make up for this with their own end padding, but a `"pill": false` widget at the outer end of a left or right section has none. It moves from 8 px inside the bar edge to 1 px past it, and further with a larger `pill-gap`.

**Impact:** a `"pill": false` widget at the outer end of a section extends past the bar edge, which matches the README's example layout. This comes from source; it was not observed on screen.

**Suggested change:** keep `Style.space(8)` for an end slot whose role is `none`, or compute the margin from the outermost drawn slot's role.

### Pills on: dragging the first widget of a pill covers the rest of it

The run's pill rectangle is a child of its first slot, and a dragged slot gets `z: 100` (`Bar.qml:1946`). While that first widget is dragged in a left, right or unanchored centre section, its pill paints over the other widgets in the same pill.

**Impact:** during the drag, the other widgets in that pill are hidden when the pill is opaque, or tinted when it is translucent. This comes from Qt's paint order; it was not observed on screen.

**Suggested change:** draw the pills in a layer behind the row or column, or skip the z raise for a slot that owns a multi-widget pill.

**Documentation:** `docs/omarchy-shell.md:389` points to `omarchy bar pills section`, but `bin/omarchy-bar` has no `pills` command at this head (#13140 adds it). The layer-rules link in `default/agents/skills/omarchy/hyprland.md` returns 404; the current page is https://wiki.hypr.land/configuring/core/rules/layer-rules/. The `hl.layer_rule` snippet itself matches the Hyprland 0.56 Lua bindings.
